President Trump on Monday announced plans for a new $15 billion steel plant in Iowa, which he said will be the largest steel plant in U.S. history.   "The steel will be mined, melted and made right here in the USA, which is something that's very unusual," he told reporters in the Oval Office.   Mesabi Metallics, a Minnesota-based company, plans to construct the plant with the goal of starting production in 2030 and eventually producing 10 million tons of steel per year.   President Trump said the project is expected to create 6,000 new construction jobs and 2,000 new manufacturing and mining jobs.   "The plant will produce some of the highest quality, most affordable steel anywhere in the world," he said. "They're going to be making it here and using it here and also shipping it outside."   The president attributed the plant's announcement to his administration's "pro-American" policies, including its 50% tariffs on foreign steel.   "Now, our steel industry is roaring back to life," he said. "Everyone's building their plant here because they don't want to pay tariffs. President Donald Trump drew attention after telling reporters that the United States has the “best poverty numbers ever,” adding that there is less poverty now than at any point in the country’s history. His comments appear to reference newly released Census Bureau data showing that the official U.S. poverty rate fell from 10.6% in 2024 to 10.2% in 2025, with about 34.5 million Americans still living below the official poverty line. Trump’s broader claim needs some context. The 2025 official poverty rate was historically low, and the child poverty rate reached a record low of 13.4%, according to the Census Bureau. However, the Supplemental Poverty Measure, which accounts for taxes, government benefits, housing costs and certain other expenses, stood at 13.1% in 2025 and was not statistically different from 2024. So the latest data show a meaningful decline in the official poverty rate, while different measures of economic hardship tell a more complicated story than the phrase “best poverty numbers ever” suggests. #democrats #uspolitics #whitehouse #corruption #poverty
